model_solution:
1. Cast Fourth Bridge Prowler (Swamp #1). ETB trigger: Servo gets -1/-1 and dies. Opponent now has no creature that can block a non-flier.
2. Cast the second Night Market Lookout (Swamp #2).
3. Activate Crew 1 on Aethersphere Harvester, tapping the first Night Market Lookout. Lookout trigger: opponent loses 1 (15), you gain 1 → Defiant Bloodlord trigger: opponent loses 1 (14). Crackdown Construct trigger: 3/3. Harvester is now an artifact creature.
4. Activate Crew 1 again, tapping the second Night Market Lookout: opponent to 13, then 12 via Bloodlord. Construct 4/4.
5. Activate Crew 1 again, tapping Fourth Bridge Prowler. Construct 5/5.
6. Activate Crew 1 again, tapping Defiant Bloodlord (its life-loss trigger still works while tapped). Construct 6/6.
7. Activate Crew 1 again, tapping the (now creature) Aethersphere Harvester itself. Construct 7/7.
8. Equip Captain's Claws to Crackdown Construct (Swamp #3). Construct 8/8, +1/+0 → 9/8.
9. Equip Captain's Claws to Fourth Bridge Prowler (Swamp #4). Construct 9/9.
10. Equip Captain's Claws back to Crackdown Construct (Swamp #5). Construct 10/10, +1/+0 → 11/10.
11. Attack with Crackdown Construct. Captain's Claws trigger: create a 1/1 Kor Ally token tapped and attacking. Neither Gloomwidow can block (both attackers lack flying) and the Servo is dead, so nothing can block.
12. Combat damage: 11 (Construct) + 1 (Kor) = 12 ≥ 12 remaining life. Opponent goes to 0 and loses.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

3281:701.3b If an effect tries to attach an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to an object or player it can’t be attached to, the Aura, Equipment, or Fortification doesn’t move. If an effect tries to attach an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to the object or player it’s already attached to, the effect does nothing. If an effect tries to attach an object that isn’t an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to another object or player, the effect does nothing and the first object doesn’t move.
4057:702.16p One Aura (Benevolent Blessing) gives the enchanted creature protection from a quality and says the effect doesn’t remove certain permanents that are “already attached to” that creature. This means that, when the protection effect starts to apply, any objects with the stated quality that are already attached to that creature (including the Aura giving that creature protection) will not be put into their owners’ graveyards as a state-based action. Other permanents with the stated quality can’t become attached to the creature. If the creature has other instances of protection from the same quality, those instances affect attached permanents as normal.

4870:702.122a Crew is an activated ability of Vehicle cards. “Crew N” means “Tap any number of other untapped creatures you control with total power N or greater: This permanent becomes an artifact creature until end of turn.”

Then I crew Harvester by tapping itself since it's untapped, bringing the Construct to 7/7, then equip the Claws across three untapped Swamps to boost it further and even pump the Prowler once, ending with the Construct at 11/10 or so. With Gloomwidow unable to block due to lacking flying and no other blockers available, an 11-power attack plus the Kor's 1 power should be enough to finish off the opponent's remaining life total, though I need to flag the crew self-tap rule as a caveat.

**Analysis**

Every point of damage has to come from a ground attacker (the two Gloomwidows can only block fliers, so Defiant Bloodlord and Aethersphere Harvester will always be blocked in the worst case), plus Night Market Lookout tap triggers (each tap = opponent loses 1, you gain 1 → Bloodlord makes them lose 1 more = 2 life). The Servo must be removed so the ground is completely open, and Crackdown Construct is the payload: every crew, equip, or energy activation gives it +1/+1.

Yahenni's Expertise (4 of your 5 mana, and it kills your own Lookout/Construct) and Fatal Push are red herrings.

Counting pumps: Fourth Bridge Prowler kills the Servo and is itself a body to crew with. Each of your four other creatures (both Lookouts, Prowler, Bloodlord) can tap to crew the Harvester once, and once the Harvester is a creature it can be tapped to pay its own Crew cost too (it doesn't need to attack – the Gloomwidows would just block it). Three Equip activations add three more pumps, +1/+0, and a Kor token.

<solution>
1. Cast Fourth Bridge Prowler (Swamp #1). ETB trigger: Servo gets -1/-1 and dies. Opponent now has no creature that can block a non-flier.
2. Cast the second Night Market Lookout (Swamp #2).
3. Activate Crew 1 on Aethersphere Harvester, tapping the first Night Market Lookout. Lookout trigger: opponent loses 1 (15), you gain 1 → Defiant Bloodlord trigger: opponent loses 1 (14). Crackdown Construct trigger: 3/3. Harvester is now an artifact creature.
4. Activate Crew 1 again, tapping the second Night Market Lookout: opponent to 13, then 12 via Bloodlord. Construct 4/4.
5. Activate Crew 1 again, tapping Fourth Bridge Prowler. Construct 5/5.
6. Activate Crew 1 again, tapping Defiant Bloodlord (its life-loss trigger still works while tapped). Construct 6/6.
7. Activate Crew 1 again, tapping the (now creature) Aethersphere Harvester itself. Construct 7/7.
8. Equip Captain's Claws to Crackdown Construct (Swamp #3). Construct 8/8, +1/+0 → 9/8.
9. Equip Captain's Claws to Fourth Bridge Prowler (Swamp #4). Construct 9/9.
10. Equip Captain's Claws back to Crackdown Construct (Swamp #5). Construct 10/10, +1/+0 → 11/10.
11. Attack with Crackdown Construct. Captain's Claws trigger: create a 1/1 Kor Ally token tapped and attacking. Neither Gloomwidow can block (both attackers lack flying) and the Servo is dead, so nothing can block.
12. Combat damage: 11 (Construct) + 1 (Kor) = 12 ≥ 12 remaining life. Opponent goes to 0 and loses.
</solution>

Note: step 7 relies on the Harvester tapping itself to pay its own Crew cost, which was legal under the Crew rules of the puzzle's era (Aether Revolt, 2017). The current Comprehensive Rules (702.122a) add the word "other" to Crew; if that step is disallowed, the same line still reaches 15 (the maximum otherwise available), one short – so the self-crew is the intended trick of the puzzle.
